subject: RFI: Dedicated inference reserve — throughput projections & burst allocation
messages:
From: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@cloudscale.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.ai>
Date: 2026-10-22T15:12:00-04:00
Subject: RFP: Dedicated inference reserve - initial questionnaire

Mina,

Attached is CloudScale's RFP worksheet for dedicated inference reserve sizing. We're looking for a firm recommendation on GPU mix, per-GPU throughput projections (tokens/sec) for the model families listed, and a reservation plan that balances cost predictability with burst capacity. Key constraints:
- 95th-percentile response latency target: 250ms for chat flows
- Models: Llama-2-Chat-70B (fp16), Open-Weights-13B (fp16), and embeddings workload (400M vectors/day)
- Typical sustained concurrency: ~120 concurrent chat sessions; peak burst up to ~5x baseline for short windows
- Compliance: must support private VPC deployment with audit logging

Deliverables we need within 10 business days: completed worksheet, a CSV of throughput assumptions, and a short write-up describing reservation strategy and fallback behavior. Can you confirm availability and whether Redwood can meet the 250ms 95th SLA under the proposed reservation?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Phillips
Head of Platform Engineering, CloudScale AI
Attachments: CSAI_RFP_worksheet.xlsx (blank)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@cloudscale.ai>
Date: 2026-10-23T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reserve - initial questionnaire

Jordan — thanks for the RFP and the clear constraints. We can meet your timeline. I started filling the worksheet and attached a draft (CSAI_RFP_worksheet_filled.xlsx) plus an initial CSV of throughput baselines (throughput_modeling_v1.csv). High-level notes up-front:
- We will present two sizing bands: Conservative (predictable monthly commit) and Elastic (lower commit + burst credits).
- Kernel-fit and sequence-length assumptions materially affect tokens/sec; I'll call out numbers for seq_len=2048 and seq_len=4096.
- We'll propose a warm spare strategy to hit 250ms 95th p for chat.

Quick clarification requests before finalizing numbers:
1) Are the chat sessions single-turn or multi-turn (average tokens/client per minute)?
2) Are you planning to use streaming token-by-token responses, or batched chunked responses?
3) Any constraints on allowed quantization (we recommend int8 or 4-bit Q4 for large models to reduce memory footprint).

Attached: CSAI_RFP_worksheet_filled.xlsx (draft), throughput_modeling_v1.csv

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@cloudscale.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-23T11:58:00-04:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reserve - initial questionnaire

Mina — answers below, thanks.
1) Multi-turn: average 6 turns per session, average request size ~600 tokens, response size ~120 tokens.
2) Streaming enabled for chat flows. Latency target is end-to-end (first token within 250ms for streamed responses).
3) Quantization: production policy allows int8; will need security sign-off for 4-bit.

Also note: embeddings job is a batch ingestion overnight window (02:00 - 06:00 UTC) but may have spikes outside that when customers reorder. Peak burst described above typically lasts 8-12 minutes.

Can you incorporate sequence-length sensitivity and provide separate columns for seq_len=2048 and seq_len=4096?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Jordan
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Phillips <jordan.phillips@cloudscale.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Dedicated inference reserve - throughput & burst allocation (draft)

Jordan — attached are the completed artifacts: CSAI_RFP_worksheet_filled.xlsx (final), throughput_modeling_v1.csv (seq_len columns included), reserve_pricing_estimate_v2.pdf (pricing + commit options), and kernel_fit_notes.txt (assumptions). Executive summary below; full detail is in the attachments.

Executive summary (short):
- Recommended reserved pool (Conservative commit): 12 x H100-80GB (bf16 preferred) + 6 x A100-80GB (fp16) + 4 x L4-48GB for embedding and 13B chat fallback. This mix balances throughput for 70B chat while keeping unit cost predictable.
- Elastic variant (lower commit): 6 x H100 + 4 x A100 + 6 x L4 + 40% burst credits.
- Throughput estimates (tokens/sec per GPU, seq_len=2048 / seq_len=4096):
  - H100-80GB: Llama-2-Chat-70B (bf16): 420 / 320 tok/s; Open-Weights-13B (fp16): 980 / 760 tok/s; embeddings batch throughput (per GPU): ~1.6M vectors/hour (depending on vector dim).
  - A100-80GB: Llama-2-Chat-70B (fp16): 270 / 210 tok/s; Open-Weights-13B (fp16): 640 / 500 tok/s; embeddings: ~1.1M vectors/hour.
  - L4-48GB: best for 13B: 120 / 90 tok/s; embeddings: ~400k vectors/hour.

Sizing rationale:
- Baseline sustained target (based on your avg request sizes and 120 concurrent sessions): ~50k tokens/sec platform-wide for chat. With the Conservative reserved pool above we estimate steady-state capacity of ~56k tok/s (seq_len=2048), leaving ~12% headroom. Add warm spares and pre-warmed KV cache to hit 95th p 250ms for streamed first-token latency.
- Burst handling: we model peak 5x baseline for 10-minute bursts every few hours; recommended policy: 2x reserved burst credits + autoscale to cloud-backed burst nodes for short windows. We include a recommended pre-warmed spare of 2 H100 nodes for immediate headroom.

Operational notes:
- Quantization: int8 is supported for both H100 and A100 with marginal accuracy trade-offs; 4-bit (Q4) can reduce memory and increase packing density but needs explicit security approval for production.
- Kernel fit: our kernel selection favors CUTLASS/Triton implementations on H100 for bf16 paths; kernel_fit_notes.txt documents microbenchmark results used to derive tokens/sec numbers.
- Cache & batching: prefix/KV caching reduces per-call token work by ~12% for multi-turn sessions; continuous batching for embeddings increases throughput ~1.7x during batch windows.

Attached files include per-GPU per-model CSV with columns: gpu_type, model_family, seq_len, tok_per_sec, concurrency_factor. Also included is pricing for reserved vs elastic blends (reserve_pricing_estimate_v2.pdf).

Next steps: please confirm which sizing band you prefer (Conservative vs Elastic). If you confirm Conservative, we'll convert the attachments to a single PDF and provide a draft purchase amendment/commit worksheet.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: CSAI_RFP_worksheet_filled.xlsx; throughput_modeling_v1.csv; reserve_pricing_estimate_v2.pdf; kernel_fit_notes.txt

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP - confirm kernel/ops assumptions

Mina — quick confirm: H100 numbers look reasonable against our internal 2048-benchmarks. Two caveats:
- Sequence-length increase to 4096 reduces end-to-end tok/sec by ~18-22% on average due to attention memory and sharded-kernel overhead. We've reflected that in the CSV.
- Long-lived KV caches (>50M tokens across sessions) will cause modest memory pressure; recommend periodic cache eviction windows (1-2x/day) for long-running sessions.

If CloudScale is comfortable with ~18% degradation when moving from 2048->4096 we are fine to lock the numbers.

-karthik
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.inference>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-10-28T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP - confirm autoscale/warm-spare plan

Mina/Karthik — quick note from ops: autoscale cooldown is 90s; cold-start for a new H100 instance (cold kernel/JIT warm) is ~180s. Two warm spare H100 nodes should cover immediate first-token latency for small bursts, but for sustained 5x bursts we recommend combining 2 warm spares + 40% burst credits (elastic nodes) and a short pre-warm window (trigger at 60s into burst). I've updated reserve_pricing_estimate_v2.pdf to reflect the warm-spare OPEX.

-Alex
